**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed)

The agreement contains no most-favoured-nation obligation in either direction:

- **Full-document sweep** — searches for "most favoured/favored nation", "favorable" and "favourable" returned no hits, and a complete read of the single section (p0000–p0074) confirms there is no MFN, benchmarking, or third-party price-matching provision.
- **Fees and Payment (p0023)** — a pure revenue-share mechanic that defers pricing to the Exhibits and sequential-liability payment timing. It imposes no duty on AP to extend Kubient terms no less favourable than those given to others.
- **Clause 1 (p0001)** — affirmatively cuts the other way: it disclaims exclusivity and expressly preserves AP's right to offer Inventory via other agents or sell to third parties. That is the opposite of an MFN burden on us, and is not something to flag against our own interest.

This places the deal at the rule's **preferred position** (no MFN obligation on Customer), so no edit is appropriate.

One point noted in the rationale rather than flagged as a deviation: because the commercial pricing lives in the Exhibits (which are incorporated by Clause 1 but not part of this document), any Exhibit or future amendment should be checked for a "most favourable rates" undertaking running against AP. A Vendor-granted MFN in AP's favour would, of course, be welcome and should be retained if offered.
